common_name: Autumn Colors Prairie Coneflower (Mixed Red-Gold Mexican Hat)
directions: Direct sow in fall or early spring on lean, well-drained soil; this seed strain reproduces true from open pollination and throws a mix of solid yellow, mahogany-red, and bicolor blooms rather than the pure yellow of the species type. Keep soil on the dry side and avoid rich, heavily amended beds, which cause floppy growth and fewer flowers on the tall, narrow ray petals surrounding the distinctive columnar brown-black center. Plants bloom the first summer from an early sowing and readily self-seed, so let a few seed heads mature each year to maintain the color mix in naturalized plantings. Deadheading extends bloom into fall but is unnecessary where a wilder, self-sustaining prairie look is wanted.

common_name: Asahi False Sunflower (Double Golden Japanese Heliopsis)
directions: Plant divisions or container-grown stock in spring in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Japanese-bred selection produces fully double, chrysanthemum-like golden-yellow blooms that hold their form longer in the vase and garden than the single-flowered species. Stake clumps in windy or partly shaded sites, since the heavy double flowers are carried on stems similar in height to the species type. Deadhead regularly through summer to keep new buds coming, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to renew vigor. It tolerates heat and humidity well and draws pollinators despite the doubled flower form reducing accessible pollen compared to the wild type.
